name: pdk-dataclasses-avroschema-etl
instr:
Since the billing service (Java) moved our topics from binary Avro to Avro JSON, our invoices and refunds decode wrong with this library. Lines and payments come back as the wrong class, messages from older or newer schema versions fail even when we pass `writer_schema`, and some numbers come back as text. Our refund models reuse the invoice models' payment, line and currency classes and don't even produce a usable schema.

Yesterday's captures are in /data/billing/ (kcat -J; the schema-version header names the writer's schema in /data/billing/schemas/). We read with invoice-v2.avsc and refund-v1.avsc, which our refund models must produce.

For dataclass (AvroModel) and pydantic (AvroBaseModel) models, `deserialize(..., serialization_type="avro-json", writer_schema=...)` should give what binary Avro gives for the same message: the same record class wherever a union holds records, the same values and defaults. Every captured message must decode that way. `serialize()` must write each union record as its own record in both encodings, and our Avro JSON must be strict JSON with every value written the way the service writes it. Both ways, a record is the one its schema names (schema_name and namespaces included), whatever models the process used before. An empty payload, broken JSON, a union label the writer's schema lacks, and text the service never writes in a float or double field all raise ValueError. Other schemas must not change.
